# THE TABLES CONFORMANCE MANIFEST (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3, §7, §16, §19).
#
# The registry every language driver reads. It is DATA: a port implements the
# driver contract in test/conformance/README.md, points it at this file, and
# the harness is the gate. Nothing here names a language.
#
# Line kinds:
#
#   unit     <key> <schema path>...
#            a compilation unit, by the key the other lines use.
#
#   instance <name> <unit> <root> <wire file>
#            one table instance, in TWO forms that must agree: the table wire
#            bytes at <wire file> (§3) and the JSON text at
#            testdata/conformance/tables/json/<name>.json (§16). The same
#            instance both ways.
#
#   report   <case> <unit> <root> <wire file>
#            bytes read by a type that did not write them — the evolution class
#            (§4). The counters are the whole expectation, and they live in
#            reports.txt keyed by <case>, because they are GENERATED and this
#            file is hand-authored.
#
#   cook     <case> <unit> <root> <dump file>
#            a cooked file (§7) — materialised by test/cookgen, which is
#            deterministic — and the canonical node dump its Open must produce,
#            byte for byte. <case> names the FIXTURE and <root> the table it is
#            opened at: one root can have more than one fixture.
#
#   block    <name> <unit> <block file>
#            a block image (§19) an Open must accept.
#
#   forgery  <name> <kind> <subject> <base> <offset> <width> <value> <extent> <verdict> <label>
#            one damaged fixture and the verdict every implementation owes it.
#            A forgery is a PATCH over a base fixture, because a patch is what a
#            person can review; the harness materialises the file, and a driver
#            only ever meets a path and the extent its caller claims.
#
# Wire files are REFERENCED where they already live rather than copied: the
# table-wire goldens are the same files test/tables/main.cpp pins.

unit tabledemo tables/examples
unit tblv1     test/tables/V1.schema
unit tblv2     test/tables/V2.schema
unit tblp1     test/tables/P1.schema
unit tblp3     test/tables/P3.schema
unit tblp2     test/tables/P2.schema
unit graphdemo tables/pointers
unit blockdemo tables/block
unit messagedemo tables/messages
unit streamdemo tables/stream
unit blobdemo  tables/blobs
unit tblm1     test/tables/M1.schema
unit tblm2     test/tables/M2.schema

instance root_full            tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin
instance root_default         tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_default.bin
instance profile_elide        tabledemo ProfileConfig testdata/wire/tables/profile_elide.bin
instance loadout_full         tabledemo LoadoutConfig testdata/wire/tables/loadout_full.bin
instance wide_blob            tabledemo WideBlob      testdata/wire/tables/wide_blob.bin
instance archive              tabledemo ArchiveConfig testdata/wire/tables/archive.bin
instance keyed_config         tabledemo KeyedConfig   testdata/wire/tables/keyed_config.bin
instance keyed_default        tabledemo KeyedConfig   testdata/wire/tables/keyed_default.bin
instance v1_cfg               tblv1     Cfg           testdata/wire/tables/v1_cfg.bin
instance v1_seams             tblv1     Cfg           testdata/wire/tables/v1_seams.bin
instance v2_cfg               tblv2     Cfg           testdata/wire/tables/v2_cfg.bin
instance v2_seams             tblv2     Cfg           testdata/wire/tables/v2_seams.bin
instance chain_value          tblp1     Chain         testdata/wire/tables/chain_value.bin
instance chain_value_empty    tblp1     Chain         testdata/wire/tables/chain_value_empty.bin
instance chain_optional       tblp3     Chain         testdata/wire/tables/chain_optional.bin
instance chain_optional_empty tblp3     Chain         testdata/wire/tables/chain_optional_empty.bin

# THE VARIABLE CLASS (§3.1), and the four shapes the numbering has to get right.
# Three carry a text (§16.7): a tree reads and writes as nested tables, and
# graph_shared is the one a tree cannot spell — one list node named from `head`,
# from `alias` and from a by-value nesting, and a diamond whose closing
# reference names a node already numbered. Four nodes held by seven slots, the
# shared two under `&node`, and the tool's own cook of these bytes agrees.
#
# graph_deep is `no-text` BY THE FORM'S OWN RULE: a chain nests in the text as
# deep as it is long (§16.7), and 260 nodes is past the depth cap every walk
# carries (§16.2), so the writer refuses it in the reference and in the tool
# alike. It rides the wire, which has no such bound.
instance graph_tree           graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_tree.bin
instance graph_shared         graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_shared.bin
instance graph_empty          graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_empty.bin
instance graph_deep           graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_deep.bin   no-text

# THE MESSAGE CLASS (§2.6): a union whose arms are tables, at three depths in
# messagedemo — ToolBody in the root, EditBody inside a transaction's edits,
# Origin inside an insert. message_ping and message_save pin the rule that a SET
# arm rides even when its body is entirely default, for a type arm and a table
# arm alike; message_empty is the elided None. streamdemo's Frame has a VARIABLE
# arm, so Feed is a region and a root pointer, and its chunk arm's chain is
# numbered through the union. message_batch is the ARRAY OF UNIONS (§3) at the
# same three depths — history counted in the root with a live None slot,
# pending fixed inside the transaction with its None element riding in place,
# origins counted inside the insert.
instance message_open         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/message_open.bin
instance message_transaction  messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/message_transaction.bin
instance message_ping         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/message_ping.bin
instance message_save         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/message_save.bin
instance message_empty        messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/message_empty.bin
instance message_batch        messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/message_batch.bin
instance message_trace        messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/message_trace.bin
instance m1_open              tblm1       Msg         testdata/wire/tables/m1_open.bin
instance m1_save              tblm1       Msg         testdata/wire/tables/m1_save.bin
instance m2_close             tblm2       Msg         testdata/wire/tables/m2_close.bin
instance m2_open              tblm2       Msg         testdata/wire/tables/m2_open.bin
instance stream_chain         streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_chain.bin
instance stream_header        streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_header.bin
instance stream_parts         streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_parts.bin
# THE WALK ORDER (§3.1), told apart: the numbering is ONE declaration-order walk
# that descends a by-value edge IN PLACE, and Feed declares its union arm before
# its pointer fields. Here the arm reaches every node first — frame.chunk.next
# is a, a.next is b, frame.chunk.links names c — and parts names the same three
# in the REVERSE order, [c, b, a], with pair naming b again. The page's walk
# numbers a, b, c as 2, 3, 4; a walk that takes the pointer fields first numbers
# c, b, a as 2, 3, 4 and writes different bytes from the same value. Every other
# seed coincides under both orders, which is exactly what a seed must not rely
# on. The wire is the TOOL's (`schema pack` of the text), and the reference is
# held to it.
instance stream_arm_first     streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_arm_first.bin

# THE BYTE BUFFER corpus (§2.5): a blob at its used size, pointed at. blob_small
# carries every field once; blob_empty holds a present blob and string of length
# zero beside null slots — two values at the empty end; blob_large is one blob
# past a 64 KiB slab. blob_shared is `no-text` BY THE FORM'S OWN RULE: a blob's
# text is a string, which has no first key to carry `&node`, so a blob two slots
# name has no spelling and the writer refuses the graph (§16.7).
instance blob_small           blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_small.bin
instance blob_empty           blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_empty.bin
instance blob_large           blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_large.bin
instance blob_shared          blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_shared.bin  no-text
# THE STRING TERMINATOR, at the two lengths that can see it (§6.3): a *string
# node carries one zero byte after its data, and the node's extent is rounded
# to the arena's alignment like every node's. At a length that is not a
# multiple of eight the rounding absorbs that byte and a region laid out
# without it is byte-identical; at 8 and at 16 it does not, so these two are
# the rows that hold the terminator answerable.
instance blob_str8            blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_str8.bin
instance blob_str16           blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_str16.bin

# THE EVOLUTION SEAMS (§4): every instance of one generation, read by the
# other. The counters are generated into reports.txt by the Go engine and are
# the expectation every backend must meet.
report v1_cfg_as_v2   tblv2 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/v1_cfg.bin
report v1_seams_as_v2 tblv2 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/v1_seams.bin
report v2_cfg_as_v1   tblv1 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/v2_cfg.bin
report v2_seams_as_v1 tblv1 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/v2_seams.bin
report p1_as_p3       tblp3 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_value.bin
report p3_as_p1       tblp1 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_optional.bin
report p1_empty_as_p3 tblp3 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_value_empty.bin
report p3_empty_as_p1 tblp1 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_optional_empty.bin

# THE POINTER SPELLING IS ITS OWN FRAMING (§3.1). T and ?T are wire-identical
# and read each other as instances above; *T rides as a u32 NODE INDEX under
# kind 17 with the body in the node table, so a reader of either other spelling
# meets a kind mismatch and a node table it cannot name. These two are the
# evolution cases that edit says exist, and the counters are the expectation.
report p2_as_p1       tblp1 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_pointer.bin
report p2_as_p3       tblp3 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_pointer.bin
report p2_empty_as_p1 tblp1 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_pointer_empty.bin
report p2_empty_as_p3 tblp3 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_pointer_empty.bin

# and the VARIABLE reader's own side of the same seam: P2 reads what P1 and P3
# wrote, meets a BODY where it declares an index, and counts it.
report p1_as_p2       tblp2 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_value.bin
report p3_as_p2       tblp2 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_optional.bin
report p1_empty_as_p2 tblp2 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_value_empty.bin
# AN ARRAY OF POINTERS read under §3.1's rules, as shared rows: three hand-built
# Feed bodies with one `parts` field each and no node table. The element kind
# 8 where the reader declares 17 is a kind mismatch and the field stays empty;
# five slots against a bound of four keep the prefix and count clamped; a slot
# naming index 7 where no node exists is malformed and THAT slot reads null,
# the array kept at its count. The bytes are fixed by this file, not generated.
report parts_elem_kind          streamdemo Feed testdata/wire/tables/parts_elem_kind.bin
report parts_count_past_bound   streamdemo Feed testdata/wire/tables/parts_count_past_bound.bin
report parts_index_out_of_range streamdemo Feed testdata/wire/tables/parts_index_out_of_range.bin
# AN ARRAY OF UNIONS read under §3's rules, as shared rows: two hand-built
# ToolMessage bodies with one `history` field each. The element kind 13 where
# the reader declares 15 is a kind mismatch and the field stays empty —
# `[N]Body` ⇄ `[N]Table` is a reported edit; an arm id no build declares reads
# as a None element, skipped by its length and counted, the slot kept live.
# The bytes are pinned by the C++ leg (test/tables/main.cpp builds them).
report batch_elem_kind   messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/batch_elem_kind.bin
report batch_unknown_arm messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/batch_unknown_arm.bin
# AN OPTIONAL ARRAY read under §2.3's rules, as shared rows: three hand-built
# ToolMessage bodies with one optional-array field each. The element kind 8
# where the reader declares 13 is a kind mismatch and the field reads ABSENT —
# its declared default, exactly as a skipped field's; four elements against a
# bound of three keep the prefix, count clamped, and the field is PRESENT — it
# rode with its own element kind; and a variant id no build names, in the FIXED
# spelling over enums, leaves that slot at None and counts it unknown while the
# field stays present. The bytes are pinned by the C++ leg
# (test/tables/main.cpp builds them).
report trace_elem_kind         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/trace_elem_kind.bin
report trace_count_past_bound  messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/trace_count_past_bound.bin
report marks_unknown_variant   messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/marks_unknown_variant.bin
# the message pair (§2.6, §4): M2 inserted `close` first, removed `save` and
# grew Open, so open's tag moved and both sides meet an arm they cannot name
report m1_open_as_m2  tblm2 Msg testdata/wire/tables/m1_open.bin
report m1_save_as_m2  tblm2 Msg testdata/wire/tables/m1_save.bin
report m2_close_as_m1 tblm1 Msg testdata/wire/tables/m2_close.bin
report m2_open_as_m1  tblm1 Msg testdata/wire/tables/m2_open.bin

block block_render blockdemo testdata/wire/tables/block_render.bin testdata/conformance/tables/block/block_render.dump
block block_padded blockdemo testdata/wire/tables/block_padded.bin testdata/conformance/tables/block/block_padded.dump

# THE COOKED FILES (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §7). The fixture itself is materialised by
# test/cookgen, which is deterministic, so what is pinned here is the canonical
# NODE DUMP: one line per node and one per leaf, the same walk in every
# language, byte-compared. A record laid out one byte differently INSIDE a node
# moves no node offset, so this is the gate the directory check cannot be.
cook Scene       graphdemo Scene    testdata/conformance/tables/cook/Scene.dump
cook Depot       graphdemo Depot    testdata/conformance/tables/cook/Depot.dump
cook Album       graphdemo Album    testdata/conformance/tables/cook/Album.dump
cook TreeNode    graphdemo TreeNode testdata/conformance/tables/cook/TreeNode.dump
cook ListNode    graphdemo ListNode testdata/conformance/tables/cook/ListNode.dump
# and the VALUED chain, which is why <case> and <root> are two columns: the five
# above are value-initialised, so their dumps lock every offset, every deref and
# every visit order and almost no VALUES. This one carries a value in every
# non-pointer leaf, so the same walk locks what a reader READS as well.
cook SceneValued graphdemo Scene    testdata/conformance/tables/cook/SceneValued.dump

# THE COOK WRITE SIDE (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §7.6): a runtime WRITES the cooked
# file and the bytes are `schema cook`'s, byte for byte, in BOTH byte orders.
# Each line names an INSTANCE the file already carries — its unit, root and wire
# are on that line and are not repeated here — and the two files the tool wrote
# from it. `make conformance-generate` writes those; they are generated, like
# the JSON texts and reports.txt, and a byte that MOVES under an unchanged
# schema is stop-the-line.
#
#   cook-write <instance> <little-endian file> <big-endian file>
#
# The big-endian half is not host-dependent: the order is a PARAMETER of the
# write, settled at cook time for the target build (§7), so every leg answers
# both halves on any host.
cook-write root_full              testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/root_full.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/root_full-be.cook
cook-write root_default           testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/root_default.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/root_default-be.cook
cook-write profile_elide          testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/profile_elide.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/profile_elide-be.cook
cook-write loadout_full           testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/loadout_full.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/loadout_full-be.cook
cook-write wide_blob              testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/wide_blob.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/wide_blob-be.cook
cook-write archive                testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/archive.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/archive-be.cook
cook-write keyed_config           testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/keyed_config.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/keyed_config-be.cook
cook-write keyed_default          testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/keyed_default.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/keyed_default-be.cook
cook-write v1_cfg                 testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v1_cfg.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v1_cfg-be.cook
cook-write v1_seams               testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v1_seams.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v1_seams-be.cook
cook-write v2_cfg                 testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v2_cfg.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v2_cfg-be.cook
cook-write v2_seams               testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v2_seams.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v2_seams-be.cook
cook-write chain_value            testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/chain_value.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/chain_value-be.cook
cook-write chain_value_empty      testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/chain_value_empty.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/chain_value_empty-be.cook
cook-write chain_optional         testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/chain_optional.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/chain_optional-be.cook
cook-write chain_optional_empty   testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/chain_optional_empty.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/chain_optional_empty-be.cook

# THE BLOCK FORGERY BATTERY as data (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §19.2), pinned from
# test/tables/block_main.cpp's eleven by test/conformance/cpp: each row is one
# word of an otherwise valid block image, resolved to a byte offset.
#
#   forgery <name> block <subject> <base> <pointer> <offset> <width> <value> <extent> <verdict> <label>
#
# <base> names the block line the image comes from; <extent> is the length the
# CALLER claims (-1: the image's own); <pointer> is 0 — every block row is read
# out of an ALIGNED base, and the column is the cook battery's.
# The harness applies the patch and hands a driver a path.
# Repin with: make conformance-pin.
forgery block_magic_foreign        block block_render block_render 0 0x0000 8 0x0                      -1 refuse a foreign magic
forgery block_magic_swapped        block block_render block_render 0 0x0000 8 0x5343484d41424c4b       -1 refuse a block of the other byte order
forgery block_build_version        block block_render block_render 0 0x0008 8 0x863a8eebc1090dc7       -1 refuse a build this one does not match
forgery block_byte_order           block block_render block_render 0 0x0010 8 0x2                      -1 refuse the other byte order in the prologue's own word
forgery block_array_unaligned      block block_render block_render 0 0x0030 8 0x141                    -1 refuse an array start not aligned for its element
forgery block_array_in_prologue    block block_render block_render 0 0x0030 8 0x0                      -1 refuse an array start inside the projection
forgery block_array_escapes        block block_render block_render 0 0x0030 8 0x783b40                 -1 refuse an array that leaves the block
forgery block_pitch                block block_render block_render 0 0x003c 4 0x60                     -1 refuse a pitch that is not this build's own
forgery block_count_past_extent    block block_render block_render 0 0x0038 4 0xfa0                200000 refuse a count whose rows leave the extent the caller passed
forgery block_count_past_maximum   block block_render block_render 0 0x0038 4 0x1388              7879488 refuse a count past the declared maximum, inside a roomy extent
forgery block_offset_overflow      block block_render block_render 0 0x0020 8 0x7fffffffffffffc0       -1 refuse an offset 64-aligned and just under 2^63 — the forgery fuzzer's find

# THE COOK FORGERY BATTERY as data (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §7, §7.4), pinned
# from test/tables/cook_main.cpp's 111 by that binary's emit-forgeries mode:
# every row is one edit to an otherwise valid cook, resolved to byte offsets
# over the fixture test/cookgen writes for this root.
#
#   forgery <name> cook <subject> <base> <pointer> <offset> <width> <value> <extent> <verdict> <label>
#
# <pointer> is the BUFFER the caller holds — 0 an aligned base, 1..63 that
# many bytes past one, `null` no buffer at all — because an unaligned base is
# a pointer fact and not a file fact. <extent> is the length the caller
# claims (-1: the file's own), and a claim SHORT of the file is a truncation.
# The three rows whose verdict is `open` are §7's own ruling written down:
# Open reads the header and points, and those three are cook-check's.
# Repin with: make conformance-pin.
forgery cook_magic_byte0               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4f4f434d4843ac             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte1               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4f4f434d48bc53             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte2               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4f4f434db74353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte3               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4f4f43b2484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte4               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4f4fbc4d484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte5               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4fb0434d484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte6               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4bb04f434d484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte7               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0xb44f4f434d484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_reversed            cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x5343484d434f4f4b             -1 refuse the magic byte-reversed: a cook of the other byte order
forgery cook_magic_block               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4c42414d484353             -1 refuse the BLOCK form's magic: a block where a cook was written

# THE HOSTILE-VALUE BATTERY (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §16.2, §16.3, §17.5): one tree
# per rule the text form states, so a divergence between the compiler's engine
# and a backend shows up as a diff rather than as a happy path that still
# passes. It moved here whole from tables/pack — it was always data, and it had
# a manifest of its own that this file now is.
#
#   json-hostile <case> <unit> <root> <tree> <verdict>
#
# <tree> is the directory `schema pack` reads, so the text is <tree>/<root>.json
# (§17). <verdict> is `refused` or the §4 report the read produces,
# <unknown>,<kind_mismatch>,<clamped>,<duplicate>,<malformed>.
#
# A case that PACKS carries one further invariant, uniform and therefore not
# spelled per row: the bytes it produces load CLEAN in the generated backend —
# report all zero — and re-save byte-identically. That half is
# test/tables/hostile_main.cpp's, which reads these very rows.
json-hostile array-past-bound             tabledemo RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/array-past-bound             0,0,2,0,false
json-hostile base64-empty                 tabledemo RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/base64-empty                 0,0,0,0,false

# THE RESERVED PREFIX (§16.7): a key beginning with `&` is how a shared node is
# named, and no declaration may take one — so a FIXED reader meeting it is not
# meeting a field it lacks. It refuses, counted, rather than skipping the key
# and reading a shared graph as a tree with an empty object at every reference.

# THE SHARING CONSTRUCT'S OWN EDGES (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §16.7), over the
# pointered root: `&node` is a LABEL — with fields after it, it defines a node
# once; alone, it names that node again; the other two readings are refused — the FIRST key of a
# pointer's object and nothing else. Three rows are not refusals, and they are the differential's
# point — both engines have to place the same graph and count the same event.

# THE WIDE SCALARS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3, §16.2): every scalar the type wire
# carries, in a table — the fixed-point family at every width and signedness,
# the 128-bit integers, each as an element and a nested field. The unit is the
# C++ reference's and the tool's; every other leg answers these ABSENT until it
# lands the kinds (§15). scalars2 is the same root as a later build reads it:
# a fixed respelled as an integer and a 128-bit narrowed to 64 (kind
# mismatches), two ranges tightened (clamps on the raw scale), two fields gone.
unit scalars     tables/scalars
unit tblscalars2 test/tables/Scalars2.schema
instance scalars_full    scalars SimState testdata/wire/tables/scalars_full.bin
instance scalars_default scalars SimState testdata/wire/tables/scalars_default.bin
instance scalars_edges   scalars SimState testdata/wire/tables/scalars_edges.bin
report scalars_full_as_2  tblscalars2 SimState testdata/wire/tables/scalars_full.bin
report scalars_edges_as_2 tblscalars2 SimState testdata/wire/tables/scalars_edges.bin
cook-write scalars_full    testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_full.cook    testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_full-be.cook
cook-write scalars_default testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_default.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_default-be.cook
cook-write scalars_edges   testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_edges.cook   testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_edges-be.cook

# the text form's rules at the wide kinds (§16.2): a fixed takes any number
# token whose value is EXACTLY representable in its Q I.F and refuses a finer
# one as the wrong shape, never rounding; out of range clamps on the raw scale;
# a magnitude past 128 bits saturates and counts; a 128-bit integer takes any
# integral token, exact past 2^53

# THE BYTE BUFFER's text rules (§2.5, §16.2): `""` and `null` are two values;
# a body that is not base64, or not a string at all, is `kind_mismatch` with
# the reference left null; and an `&node` label inside a value a mismatch
# SKIPPED defines nothing, so a later reference to it is one more mismatch.
json-hostile blob-empty-string            blobdemo Catalog testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/blob-empty-string            0,0,0,0,false
